surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Canadiens edge the Maple Leafs
paras: The Maple Leafs’ Gavin McKenna played his first NHL game. Kirill Marchenko made his Maple Leafs debut, after four seasons with the Blue Jackets, and picked up an assist. William Nylander opened the scoring for the Leafs just 48 seconds into the game, but Josh Anderson tied it up for Montréal midway through the first. Zachary Bolduc put the Canadiens ahead for good early in the second. Alexandre Carrier made it 3-1 midway through the third, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Nylander scored his second of the night with a little over four minutes left to pull the Maple Leafs within one.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Jakub Dobeš made 26 saves for the Canadiens, and Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 21 of 24. The Canadiens improved to 1-0-0, and the Maple Leafs fell to 0-1-0.

items.text: It was the first game of the season for both teams, and the Maple Leafs lost their home opener.
The Canadiens have beaten the Maple Leafs four straight times, going back to last season.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
